readerTitle: Vanguard got cheap by saying no to what rivals relied on
caseNote: 실제 기업 (Vanguard, 1975~1977년의 결정과 이후 결과, Fidelity의 2018년 무보수 인덱스 펀드) + 가상 적용 (점심 식당)
insight: 진짜 저비용은 가격표에서 나오지 않는다. 경쟁사가 기대고 있는 것을 포기한 데서 나온다. 그래서 따라 하기 어렵다.
misconception: 저비용 전략은 같은 일을 더 싸게 하는 것이다. 수수료나 가격만 낮추면 된다.

sources.text: Bogle, J. C. (2018). Stay the Course: The Story of Vanguard and the Index Revolution. Wiley. (1975년 설립, 상호 소유 구조, 1976년 인덱스 펀드 공모, 1977년 판매 수수료 폐지)
Vanguard, company history ("Our history" page on vanguard.com)
Fidelity Investments press release (August 2018): launch of zero expense ratio index funds
Porter, M. (1996). What Is Strategy? Harvard Business Review.

factChecks.note: 첫 인덱스 펀드(First Index Investment Trust, 이후 Vanguard 500 Index Fund) 공모 금액 약 1,100만 달러, 목표 1억 5,000만 달러라는 수치는 Bogle의 저서와 다수 언론에 나옵니다. 게시 전 Bogle(2018) 원문으로 다시 확인하세요.
"Bogle's Folly"라는 별명은 널리 인용되지만 누가 처음 썼는지는 확인하지 않았습니다. 카드에는 "critics called it"으로만 적었습니다.
1977년 2월 판매 수수료(load) 폐지와 브로커 판매망 중단은 Vanguard 공식 역사와 Bogle 저서에 나옵니다. 정확한 날짜는 카드에 쓰지 않고 연도만 적었습니다.
Vanguard가 광고비를 적게 썼다는 점은 정성적으로만 서술했습니다. 구체적 금액은 쓰지 않았습니다.
최근 몇 년 고객 서비스·웹사이트에 대한 불만 보도는 여러 언론(WSJ 등)에 나왔지만, 특정 수치나 사건은 카드에 쓰지 않았습니다. 게시 전 대표 기사 1건을 출처로 추가하는 것을 권장합니다.
대형 운용사들이 고수수료 액티브 펀드 이익 때문에 저가 인덱스 대응이 늦었다는 설명은 업계에서 흔한 해석입니다. 단정적 사실이 아닌 일반적 설명으로 적었습니다.

cards.title: A fund that promised not to beat the market
body: In 1976, a tiny company called Vanguard launched a fund for ordinary investors with an odd pitch. It would not try to beat the market. It would simply copy it, as cheaply as possible.

The launch raised about $11 million, far below its $150 million goal. Critics called it "Bogle's Folly," after founder Jack Bogle. Vanguard later became one of the largest fund companies in the world.

image.label: A small piggy bank beside a towering stack of coins
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 작은 돼지 저금통 하나가 거대한 동전 탑 옆에 서 있고, 저금통에서 동전 탑까지 성장 화살표가 이어짐. 실제 회사 로고, 배 모양 엠블럼, 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: It's 1977. Your funds are sold by brokers.
body: Like most fund companies then, Vanguard's funds reached investors through brokers. Investors paid a sales charge on each purchase, and that charge paid the brokers.
Your whole idea is low cost. But brokers are how customers find you. What do you do?

options.text: Keep the brokers and the sales charge. You need the reach
options.feedback: You keep a proven way to find customers. But every dollar of sales charge works against the one promise that makes you different.

options.text: Drop the sales charge and the brokers. Sell directly to investors
options.feedback: You make the low-cost promise real, but you give up your main sales channel overnight. That's a true trade-off, and it's what Vanguard did.

options.text: Keep the brokers but cut the sales charge in half
options.feedback: It looks like a fair middle path. But you'd be a bit cheaper and a bit less attractive to brokers, without fully owning either position.

cards.title: Vanguard cut off its own sales force.
body: In 1977, Vanguard dropped sales charges and stopped selling through the broker network. Investors had to come to Vanguard directly.
It was a risky bet. Brokers had no reason to recommend a fund that paid them nothing. Growth had to come from investors who sought Vanguard out, often by word of mouth.
For years, growth was slow. But the cost advantage was now built into how the business worked, not just into a price.

cards.title: A trade-off is what makes a position hard to copy.
body: A **trade-off** is a choice where getting more of one thing means getting less of another. You can't have both.
Vanguard didn't just charge less. It gave up things its rivals depended on:
list: **Star managers:** index funds copy the market instead of paying for stock pickers
**Heavy advertising:** it spent little, compared with rivals
**Outside owners:** its funds own the company, so there are no outside shareholders to pay
cards.callout: Each "no" removed a cost. Together, they made low cost a structure, not a discount.
cards.softwareNote: A self-serve software company with no sales team, little paid marketing and one simple plan can price far below rivals. The low price lasts only because those costs were never there.

cards.title: Copying Vanguard meant hurting yourself.
body: Many large fund companies earned high fees from funds run by star managers and sold by brokers. A cheap index fund could pull money away from their own most profitable products.
So matching Vanguard wasn't only an operations problem. It meant giving up profits, upsetting brokers and admitting that their managers might not beat the market.
This is the core of a trade-off: **what protects you is what your rivals would have to give up.**

image.label: A balance scale: low fees on one side, brokers and star managers on the other
image.brief: 인포그래픽. 저울 한쪽에 "Low fees", 다른 쪽에 "Brokers", "Star managers", "Big ad budgets" 블록. 한쪽을 올리면 다른 쪽이 반드시 내려가는 모습. 실제 로고 없음.

cards.title: Trade-offs cost something, and prices can be matched.
body: Low prices alone don't stay unique. In 2018, Fidelity launched index funds with zero fees. What's hard to copy is the structure behind the price, not the price itself.

Saying no also has a real cost. In recent years, some Vanguard customers have publicly complained about its service and website. When you keep costs low, some customers will feel what you chose not to spend.
A good trade-off is one you accept on purpose, knowing who will leave.

cards.title: Now it's a lunch spot.
body: You run a busy lunch counter near offices. Your prices are the lowest in the area, thanks to a short menu, counter ordering and no table service.
Customers say they'd love table service and a longer menu. A nearby restaurant offers both at higher prices. What do you do?

options.text: Add table service and five new dishes to win more customers
options.feedback: You'd please some customers, but you'd take on staff and stock costs that eat the low prices your regulars come for.

options.text: Keep the model and make the speed and price obvious to customers
options.feedback: You lose diners who want service, but you protect the costs your rival can't cut without changing its whole business.

options.text: Keep counter service, but add a longer menu
options.feedback: Cheaper than table service, but more dishes mean more waste and slower lines. Test one item before adding five.

cards.title: Low cost is built from things you refuse to do.
body: Vanguard's price advantage came from giving up brokers, star managers and outside owners. Rivals couldn't match it without giving up the same things.
**Try it today:** list three things your competitors spend money on that you could stop doing. For each, write down which customers you would lose.
